title: Craig reaxiomatization

based_on.title: Craig’s Theorem
based_on.pages: Undated two-page note; §1, p.1, mathematical reaxiomatization argument

summary: Replace enumerable first-order axioms by a decidable padded set with the same models and consequences.
abstract: An algorithm may list a theory’s axioms even when no algorithm decides whether a proposed sentence is one of them. Craig reaxiomatization replaces the axiom set by a decidable set that proves exactly the same sentences and has exactly the same models. At each finite stage, collect the axioms seen so far into one conjunction, using a tautology when none has appeared. Repeating that conjunction records its position syntactically. The numerical code of a proposed axiom bounds every position that could produce it, giving a finite membership test. The construction applies to empty and inconsistent axiom sets and preserves the decision status of the entire consequence set.
